raw_response:
I have a lot of land this year, so I cannot gamble on one crop only. Sweetpotato is my main crop because that is the system I know best and it sells well when the stand is good. But I still keep some maize and millet. Maize gives me a steady grain crop, and millet can sit on the lighter land with less water and less fuss. I do not read books for this. I do what I have seen work on my own fields and what the other capable farmers around here do. With 349.9 mu, family labor is not enough, so I use machines where I can and hire people for the busy days. I have a well, so I am not fully depending on the sky, but pumping water costs money, so I will not water unless the crop really needs it.

For sweetpotato, I will put the better, looser land into it and make it the biggest area. I will ridge the land, put manure or compound fertilizer underneath, and plant slips around late April into May when the soil is warm. I do not want to be too stingy on potash there, because sweetpotato without enough fertilizer makes small roots. For maize, I will use hybrid seed and plant after the ground warms, around late April to early May. I will give it a base fertilizer and one topdressing when it is growing fast. For millet, I use less money. That crop can handle poorer ground better, so I put it on the drier plots and keep the fertilizer lighter. If the year turns dry, I protect sweetpotato and maize first, and millet can take a harder life.
